narrative:
The model estimated your chance of bad credit at 34.0%, and under the bank’s lending rules that risk was high enough to deny the application. This does not mean you are certain to default; it means the model found a combination of signals that made repayment look less secure than required.

The strongest factor was your checking account status: it is currently below zero DM. That is a meaningful warning sign because most approved applicants have no negative checking balance (59.2%) and only 12.6% are in the below-zero category. This factor pushed the prediction most strongly toward bad credit. Two other factors worked in your favour: your installment rate is 2% of disposable income, below the approved average of about 2.99%, and your stated purpose of a used car also reduced the estimated risk. Even so, those positive signals were not enough to offset the checking-account concern, so the application was declined.

To improve a future application, bring the checking account back to a non-negative balance and keep it there for several months. Consider requesting a smaller amount or shorter repayment period, since your request is well above the approved average, and provide updated proof of savings, employment and housing stability. A lower requested amount and cleaner account conduct may make your next application more competitive.
